Mixed-effects fit by marginal maximum likelihood

Source: R/EM.R
em.Rd

Fits a mixed-effects model: the random effects that insert() with effect formulas put into the parameter transformation are integrated out, and the fixed parameters and the hyperparameters of the random effects are estimated by maximizing the marginal likelihood.

A group, a level of the grouping of a random term such as a patient or a cell line, may own several conditions, which share the random effects of the group. Normal, spike-and-slab and Dirichlet-process random effects of one grouping may be combined. Random terms over several groupings, nested or crossed, are normal and integrated per connected component of the conditions.

Methods:

"focei"

Laplace approximation at the conditional modes with the exact derivative of the volume term. The default, and the method for spike-and-slab and Dirichlet-process random effects (at most 14 groups) and for several groupings.

"quadrature"

adaptive sparse-grid quadrature around the modes, started from the FOCEI fit; section Quadrature.

"laplaceEM"

ECM on the Laplace approximation with the covariance-corrected update of Omega.

"saem"

stochastic-approximation EM, also for Dirichlet-process random effects; section SAEM.

Usage

em(
  obj,
  random,
  init = NULL,
  fixed = NULL,
  method = c("focei", "quadrature", "laplaceEM", "saem"),
  control = list(),
  cores = 1L,
  verbose = TRUE,
  sparse = "auto"
)

Arguments

obj

Objective of the data, normL2() or normT() of the model g * x * p, without terms for the random effects.

random

The random effects, randomEffects() of the parameter transformation or of p.

init

Named numeric start with the parameters of obj that are neither random effects nor created by the effect formulas (those start at 0). It may also set those and the hyperparameters: omega_<a>_<a>, the log of the diagonal entry of the Cholesky factor of Omega (the log standard deviation of an uncorrelated random effect), and omega_<a>_<b>, the entry in row a and column b below the diagonal, with a and b the stems of the random effects without eta_, as in omega_cl_cl; prob_* and tau_* (spike and slab), concentration_* and tau_* (Dirichlet process), named <kind>_<grouping> and numbered _1, _2, ... where a grouping has several blocks. An em fit as init gives the start: the estimates, fixed values and random effects of that fit, without those it set to 0, and with sparse random effects the inner modes.

fixed

Named numeric of parameters held fixed.

method

"focei" (default), "quadrature", "laplaceEM" or "saem".

control

List of options; other entries are an error.

sd

start of the standard deviations of the random effects, default 0.3.

innerControl

the trust region of the modes; it stops where the Newton step is below steptol, default 1e-8.

trustControl

the outer trust region; it stops where the predicted change of -2 log L is below mtol, default 1e-5.

secondOrderCorrection

the derivative of the volume term, default TRUE.

derivMode

how FOCEI gets the second derivatives of the volume term: "forward-reverse" (default), sweeps for models built with derivMode = c("forward", "reverse", "forward-reverse"), or "forward-forward", the second-order sensitivities of models built with deriv2 = TRUE. Without the mode asked for the fit takes the other, with a message.

boundary

the largest rise of -2 log L at which a variance is set to 0, default 0.1, FALSE for none. With one grouping and several blocks, a normal random effect that forms a block alone and whose standard deviation ends below 0.1 is dropped and the fit repeated from the estimates; where -2 log L rises by at most boundary, that fit is returned and names the hyperparameter in boundary.

quadrature, saem, sparseFit

lists of the sections Quadrature, SAEM and Sparse random effects.

cores

Number of cores over the groups and conditions inside the fit; with 1 (default) no threads are started.

verbose

Logical; print the progress of the iterative methods.

sparse

"auto" (default), TRUE or FALSE: the outer trust region of FOCEI over normal random effects on the sparse Gauss-Newton Hessian. "auto" decides as trust() does.

Value

An object of class em with, among others:

argument, value, gradient, hessian

the estimates, -2 log L of the marginal likelihood with gradient and Hessian (a sparse Matrix on the sparse path, NULL with spike-and-slab or Dirichlet-process random effects); on the sparse path lowrank, the part of the Hessian kept apart (see objlist()).

information

with spike-and-slab random effects the empirical information that gives the standard errors: G / (G - 1) times the sum of the outer products of the centered scores of the G groups, plus half the Hessian of the conditions without random effects.

converged, iterations
Omega, omega

the covariance of the normal random effects, their standard deviations and correlations with standard errors.

random

per group the modes with conditional standard errors; for spike-and-slab and Dirichlet-process random effects also the cluster, 0 for the population value, and the posterior probability p0 of a deviation of 0; a column data where a sparse random effect reaches no data of the group; such an effect rests at 0 with the prior.

slab

the hyperparameters of the spike-and-slab and Dirichlet-process blocks.

valueSE

the standard error of value where it comes from importance sampling.

coupling

"expectationConsistent" where a group needed it, else NULL.

boundary

the hyperparameters set to 0, see control.

etaModes, etaSE, shrinkage
certificate

with method "quadrature" per group the importance-sampling check at the estimate, section Quadrature.

Methods: print, summary, coef, vcov, confint, logLik, residuals, predict, plot.

Quadrature

Method "quadrature" alternates between placing the nodes around the modes at the current parameters and one trust step over every parameter on these frozen nodes. The nodes of the mu-referenced fixed effects are frozen in phi = X beta + eta. Entries of control$quadrature:

tol

allowed change of -2 log L by the next level, default 0.1, split over the groups; each group takes the lowest level from the current stage of the group up within tol / G and never a lower one than before. Inf keeps the levels of the stages.

levels

the stages, default K + 1 with K the number of random effects of a group; level K + s integrates polynomials of total degree 2 s + 1 exactly.

maxLevel

highest level, default K + 8.

tolDecrement

a stage ends when a Newton step on the rebuilt nodes would lower -2 log L by less than this, default 1e-4, or than the nodes resolve.

maxEcmPerStage, cm1Control, maxCm1Iter

rebuilds per stage (default 10), trust() settings and iterations of a step (default 30).

pruneTol

nodes whose weight lies this much in log below the largest are dropped, default Inf.

certificate

FALSE, or a list of points (default 256) and seed (default 1): importance sampling at the estimate from a t5 proposal at the mode of each group. A group is flagged where the two -2 log L differ by more than three standard errors plus the error the level of the group allows, or the Pareto shape of the weights exceeds 0.7.

epsEcm, maxEcm

for "laplaceEM": the extrapolated distance to the fixed point at which it stops, default 1e-5, and the iteration limit.

SAEM

Metropolis draws of the random effects by random-walk and independence proposals at the conditional modes, Robbins-Monro averages of their sufficient statistics, the mu-referenced fixed effects and Omega in closed form, the other parameters by Newton steps on averaged quadratic models. Entries of control$saem:

nBurnin, nEM

at most that many burn-in and averaging iterations, default 200 and 300.

nMcmc, nLaplace

random-walk and independence steps per iteration, default 3 each.

laplaceEvery, laplaceScale

iterations between refreshes of the modes, default 5, and the factor of the proposal covariance, default 1.5.

window, mcTol

the burn-in ends when no parameter has a significant slope over the last window iterations (default 25), the averaging when the expected rise of -2 log L from the Monte Carlo error is below mcTol (default 0.05).

particles

with Dirichlet-process random effects the particles of the sequential importance sampling of -2 log L, default 500.

cm1Control

trust() settings of the Newton steps of the other parameters, default one iteration per SAEM iteration.

With Dirichlet-process random effects a Gibbs sweep draws the clusters of the groups (Neal 2000, algorithm 8), the averaging runs nEM iterations, and the reported clusters are the most frequent partition of the late draws.

Sparse random effects

With spike-and-slab or Dirichlet-process random effects the parameters and hyperparameters move in one trust region. The integral of a group is exact where the data couple none of the factors and the sum over the subsets of the spike-and-slab random effects of the group stays within a budget of nodes; else it is the expectation consistent (EC) approximation, and a trial point at which EC does not converge is a failed evaluation. Entries of control$sparseFit:

maxOuter

iterations of the trust region, default 200.

trustControl

the trust() settings; ftol, mtol and gtol of the tolControl there also end the search of the modes (else 1e-10).

See also

msem(), randomEffects(), insert(); the guide chapters Nonlinear mixed-effects models and Sparse deviations, the methods articles Marginal likelihood of mixed-effects models and Sparsity priors.

Examples

# \donttest{
## Theophylline, 12 subjects: one-compartment model with first-order absorption in closed
## form, log parameters with a normal random intercept per subject, additive error
th <- datasets::Theoph
th$Subject <- as.character(th$Subject)
subjects <- unique(th$Subject)
data <- as.datalist(data.frame(name = "y", time = th$Time, value = th$conc, sigma = NA_real_,
                               condition = th$Subject))
## second derivatives forward over reverse, the default of em()
dm <- c("forward", "reverse", "forward-reverse")
x <- Xt()
g <- Y(c(y = "amt * Ka / (V * Ka - Cl) * (exp(-Cl / V * time) - exp(-Ka * time))"),
       states = "time", modelname = "theoph_obs", compile = FALSE, derivMode = dm,
       outdir = tempdir())
#> Overwriting: /tmp/RtmpZujll1/theoph_obs.cpp
err <- Y(c(y = "sigma_add"), g, attachInput = FALSE, modelname = "theoph_err", compile = FALSE,
         derivMode = dm, outdir = tempdir())
#> Overwriting: /tmp/RtmpZujll1/theoph_err.cpp
## one condition per subject with the subject dose; the effect formula replaces each log parameter
## by an intercept plus a random effect per subject
doses <- tapply(th$Dose * th$Wt, th$Subject, `[`, 1)[subjects]
trafo <- branch(define(NULL, "x <- x", x = c("Ka", "V", "Cl", "amt", "sigma_add")),
                table = data.frame(ID = subjects, dose = doses, row.names = subjects))
trafo <- insert(trafo, "amt <- dose", dose = dose)
trafo <- insert(trafo, "x <- exp(x)", x = c("Ka", "V", "Cl", "sigma_add"))
p <- P(insert(trafo, Ka + V + Cl ~ 1 + (1 | ID)), method = "explicit", compile = FALSE,
       modelname = "theoph_p", derivMode = dm, outdir = tempdir())
compile(g, err, p, output = tempfile("theoph"))
#> using C++ compiler: g++ [-O2 -DNDEBUG -w -fPIC]
#> reusing 14 unchanged object(s)
obj <- normL2(data, g * x * p, errmodel = err)
init <- c(Ka = 0, V = 3, Cl = 0.7, sigma_add = log(0.5))

## FOCEI fit, the estimates and the random effects per subject
fit <- em(obj, randomEffects(p), init = init)
fit
#> EM (focei): -2 log L 359.403186, converged TRUE, 10 iterations, 12 groups
#>          Ka           V          Cl   sigma_add omega_Ka_Ka   omega_V_V 
#>   0.4638825   3.4597479   1.0121568  -0.3647014  -0.4552240  -1.9774269 
#> omega_Cl_Cl 
#>  -1.3361153 
#> Random effects:
#>  type eta1 eta2  estimate         se
#>    sd   Ka   Ka 0.6343058 0.14972302
#>    sd    V    V 0.1384250 0.04075699
#>    sd   Cl   Cl 0.2628648 0.06586477
summary(fit)
#> EM summary (focei): -2 log L 359.403186, converged TRUE, 10 iterations
#>   without the 2 pi constant of the data (NONMEM OBJ): 116.803413
#> 
#> Parameters:
#>             estimate      se rsePct
#> Ka            0.4639 0.19180 41.350
#> V             3.4600 0.04718  1.364
#> Cl            1.0120 0.08333  8.233
#> sigma_add    -0.3647 0.07268 19.930
#> omega_Ka_Ka  -0.4552 0.23600 51.850
#> omega_V_V    -1.9770 0.29440 14.890
#> omega_Cl_Cl  -1.3360 0.25060 18.750
#> Standard errors without the curvature of the prediction in the random effects within the volume term (forward over reverse; deriv2 = TRUE gives the full one)
#> 
#> Random effects:
#>  type eta1 eta2 estimate      se
#>    sd   Ka   Ka   0.6343 0.14970
#>    sd    V    V   0.1384 0.04076
#>    sd   Cl   Cl   0.2629 0.06586
#> 
#> Shrinkage: eta_Ka = 0.018, eta_V = 0.103, eta_Cl = 0.039 
fit$omega
#>   type eta1 eta2  estimate         se
#> 1   sd   Ka   Ka 0.6343058 0.14972302
#> 2   sd    V    V 0.1384250 0.04075699
#> 3   sd   Cl   Cl 0.2628648 0.06586477
head(fit$random)
#>   group eta parameter        mode        se
#> 1     1  Ka  eta_Ka_1  0.08621976 0.1515854
#> 2     2  Ka  eta_Ka_2  0.19818408 0.1725709
#> 3     3  Ka  eta_Ka_3  0.37186008 0.1810720
#> 4     4  Ka  eta_Ka_4 -0.28173371 0.1640986
#> 5     5  Ka  eta_Ka_5 -0.04271272 0.1461175
#> 6     6  Ka  eta_Ka_6 -0.38568935 0.2043190

## quadrature started from the FOCEI estimates, and SAEM
fitQ <- em(obj, randomEffects(p), init = fit, method = "quadrature", verbose = FALSE)
fitS <- em(obj, randomEffects(p), init = init, method = "saem", verbose = FALSE)
c(focei = fit$value, quadrature = fitQ$value, saem = fitS$value)
#>      focei quadrature       saem 
#>   359.4032   360.7548   360.7588 
# }
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## Ka and Cl with correlated random effects, V with a spike-and-slab one: a second transformation
p2 <- P(insert(trafo, Ka + Cl ~ 1 + (1 | p | ID), V ~ 1 + (1 | gr(ID, dist = spikeSlab()))),
        method = "explicit", compile = FALSE, modelname = "theoph_p2", derivMode = dm,
        outdir = tempdir())
compile(p2, output = tempfile("theoph"))
fit2 <- em(normL2(data, g * x * p2, errmodel = err), randomEffects(p2), init = init)
fit2$omega
fit2$slab
AIC(fit, fit2)
} # }
